claim: Let \(\alpha>0\), let \(X_\alpha=H^0_{v_\alpha}(\mathbb D)\) with \(v_\alpha(z)=(1-|z|)^\alpha\), and let \(N\ge3\), distinct positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_N\), and nonzero complex scalars \(a_1,\ldots,a_N\) be given. For \(T=\sum_{j=1}^N a_j C_{z^{m_j}}\), where \(C_\phi f=f\circ\phi\), the essential norm \(\|T\|_e=\inf_{K\in\mathcal K(X_\alpha)}\|T-K\|\) is exactly \[\|T\|_e=\sum_{j=1}^N |a_j|m_j^{-\alpha}.\] The upper bound follows from the exact single-symbol essential norm and subadditivity; the reverse bound follows from a bounded weakly-null family of boundary peaks at pairwise distinct points \(\zeta^{m_j}\), which makes all cross terms vanish and each diagonal term contribute \(|a_j|m_j^{-\alpha}\).

integrity.proof_basis: Analytic proof with explicit boundary-peak sequence and exact single-operator essential-norm formula.

Full text of the 2012 essential-norm paper

scientific_limitations: The result is limited to finite sums with N >= 3, distinct positive monomial exponents, nonzero coefficients, and the little growth space H^0_v on the disk with v(z)=(1-|z|)^alpha, alpha>0.
No assertion is made for arbitrary symbols, infinite sums, or other weights.

A 2009 paper on differences of weighted composition operators is a close antecedent; its full text was not obtained in this run, leaving a residual prior-art risk for any broader finite-sum statement.
title: Exact essential norms of finite monomial-composition sums on \(H^0_{v_\alpha}\)
